evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'Just need to ask some questions about it may take about ten to fifteen minutes if this is a good time.' — frames the time-box but does not fully deliver the 'quote you can depend on' promise or wait for explicit yes before moving forward.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Joanna: 'Of course, aside from the pricing do you have any other important concerns that you also want to discuss on this call?' — asked, but after she already said 'we received your quotation request' and began the call setup, so this comes after initial framing rather than before any probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised no concerns (said 'No' to the agenda question), so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns raised, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Gathered: move date (Oct 16, Friday), origin/destination addresses, property type (2-story townhome, 1800 sq ft), that all items are downstairs, specific furniture (Peloton, dressers), box count (~30), packing status (pre-packed), parking accessibility at both ends. Missing: walking distance from truck, additional rooms/living spaces detail, special considerations beyond what was stated.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Joanna: 'Everything's all packed good to go or do you need help packing as well?' — asked directly.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Joanna: 'In terms of boxes, how many boxes in tots are we looking at, do you think it's gonna be more than 3040?' — asked.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'So there's an estimated budget of $590 to 693' — anchored range provided. Personalized by: Friday rate ($206/hr for two movers via Fort Worth branch), 2.5–3 hour estimate, travel time factored, customer's specific light load (minimal furniture, mostly boxes/totes).

Two-and-a-half hour minimum and 15-minute increments disclosed. 'We only start the time once we arrive at your current home' and 'can have us for as long as you need us.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moves directly from estimate into Two Promises section without checking if the price feels fair or holding silence.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Joanna: 'On time guarantee if we run late, we provide discounts for your move.' — fully covers the discount framing without ambiguity.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Joanna: 'We will also include our no worries, damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair, replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages' — mentions $2,000 and no hidden fees, but does NOT explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print,' which are the explicit framing calls. Partial.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Joanna does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. No explicit closing of the Two Promises loop.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep skips Section 6 entirely.

If you're ready to go ahead with the booking, just send us a response or give us a call whichever works for you.' This provides an out (email/call later instead of committing now), so 'with_out' applies.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Email address confirmed (corrected twice: E-K-Galaviz, then V-I-Z). Date confirmed (Oct 16). No phone number, arrival window, crew size, or destination address details re-confirmed at booking stage. No crew notes on customer concerns documented.

top_strength: Joanna gathered robust logistics details through natural follow-up questions, learning the full scope of items to move, pre-packing status, and site accessibility in both locations, which allowed her to anchor a personalized estimate range with confidence.
coaching_note: Section 6 (Concerns Again) is completely missing — add a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' before the ask, and always confirm 'Does that feel fair?' after pricing before moving to Two Promises, then close the loop and check for final concerns before asking for the business.
